title: Rise Design Automation at DAC 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: At DAC 2026 Rise Design Automation showed AI-powered High Level Synthesis tools, IPCreate and IPTransform, that go from specification to HLS to RTL (and back), claiming a million gates per week, 30x faster simulation and up to 100x faster verification, using grounded AI skills rather than naive LLM code generation.

insights.claim: Rise Design Automation added an AI-powered flow that goes from specification to a High Level Synthesis model to an RTL model, using HLS to gain simulation speed, performance and capacity after overcoming earlier QOR and timing challenges.
insights.speaker: Ellie Burns
insights.so_what: Raising the design abstraction with AI targets the speed and capacity limits of hand-written RTL.

insights.claim: Using Rise's higher-level EDA tools, an engineer can create about a million gates in a week from a specification, which is not possible with hand-written RTL coding.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Large claimed productivity leap over conventional RTL design.

insights.claim: IPCreate takes a specification or MathWorks models and generates C++, SystemC or SystemVerilog models then synthesizes technology-optimized RTL, while IPTransform goes the other way from RTL to an HLS model and specification, checking claims against the spec.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Bidirectional spec-RTL flow provides a single higher-abstraction source of truth.

insights.claim: Rise's high-level models run 30X faster than RTL models, enabling larger AI-enabled systems and fewer required emulators.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Higher-abstraction simulation can reduce dependence on expensive emulation.
insights.quote: The high level models are 30X faster than RTL models.

themes.theme: Grounded AI, not naive LLM generation

insights.claim: Rise's IPCreate and IPTransform were written by humans plus some LLM-generated code using tools like Claude Code, but naively using a tool like Claude to go from specification to a high-level model can produce unsynthesizable models or hallucinations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Grounding and purpose-built skills, not raw LLM code generation, are what make agentic EDA reliable.

insights.claim: Rise uses purpose-built AI skills grounded in a curated hardware knowledge base to drive its agentic AI for HLS and EDA, and users can add their own skills to extend the tools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A curated knowledge base is the moat that constrains AI output to synthesizable results.

insights.claim: Using a human in the loop, Rise's tools created an IO MMU block for a RISC-V system in one hour, a block that would take an RTL expert months, and the generated RTL is human-readable with line references and preserved signal names.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Concrete example quantifying the claimed months-to-hours design acceleration.

insights.claim: Rise properly handles advanced nodes like 5nm and 3nm with accurate timing, integrates RTL synthesis inside the HLS flow, and enables verifying chips up to 100X faster than other methods.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Advanced-node timing support plus a 100x verification claim broaden applicability to leading-edge designs.
